C.1 VALLEY FORGE NATIONAL HISTORICAL PARK (VAFO) Valley Forge is the place where George Washington and the Continental Army took refuge during the winter of 1777-1778. Today the park protects 3,500 acres of meadows, woodlands, historic landscapes, and monuments commemorating the resolve of the Revolutionary War generation and honoring the power of people to pull together, overcome adversity, and find renewal through transformation. For more information, please visit VAFO’s website at: Valley Forge National Historical Park (U.S. National Park Service) C.2 BACKGROUND Valley Forge National Historical Park (VAFO) has two locations, Park Administration Building and the HQ Train Station that are in need of upgraded fire and security alarm panels to ensure they are up to date and within the required codes. The facility must enable cohorts to remain physically separate and prevent unnecessary “mixing.” The Contractor shall also ensure that if staff must engage with multiple cohorts, extra precautions are taken to avoid the potential spread of infectious diseases, such as the contractor seeking to avoid mixing staff across cohorts. The contractor must supply adequate personal protective equipment to all staff on-site. Contractors must provide regular updates to ORR regarding the mental and physical health of children in isolation. Emergency Services Facility Provide office for emergency services staff and equipment adjacent to paved area for emergency vehicles. Warehouse: Provide warehouse space necessary for and maintenance activities. Warehouse can be on the campus or offsite and shall be capable of storing hazardous or flammable chemicals. Campus Security Requirements Provide an 8-foot-high perimeter fence around the campus. Provide screening on fences to block lines of sight into the campus where views from outside the campus are not obscured. Provide VSS coverage (equipment must meet 48 CFR 52.204-25 requirements) of screening checkpoints, exits, loading docks, lobbies, facility perimeter, parking areas, sensitive interior areas, personnel and vehicle entrances and other potential access points. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible Offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors will be used to evaluate offers: Price: The price will be evaluated based on the total of all contract line items. Background This document defines the design and fabrication requirements for three items: a stationary liquid helium dewar, two transportable liquid helium dewars, and interconnection plumbing between the dewars that allow the transportable dewars to be filled from the stationary liquid helium dewar and a separate existing stationary liquid helium dewar. 1.1. Operational Concept The dewars and associated hardware will be manufactured by th

a NASA facility in Sandusky, OH . Upon arrival in Sandusky, the stationary dewar will be lifted onto a platform to elevate it and the two stingers will be inserted into the two stationary dewars . As a NASA provided helium liquefier produces liquid helium and fills the two stationary dewars, occasionally, the transportable dewars will be connected to the interconnect piping and filled. The transportable dewars will then be taken to a liquid helium user and the helium will be returned as high pressure gas via means outside the scope of this procurement. 1.2. The Postbox is an online submission facility which allows buyers to receive responses from suppliers electronically in a secure environment. Responses are submitted through the portal and held in the secure Postbox until the deadline for responses has expired. Nominated members of the buyer organisation then unlock the Postbox to access the submissions. The Postbox can be used for the receipt of PQQs, tender responses, Quick Quote submissions and all supporting documents. A full audit trail is kept of all access to the Postbox and a complete record of all supplier submissions is stored. Please note: Before you can use the postbox you must record your interest in a notice. This search resulted in three (3) vendors: Wonderful Water, Diamond Drinking Water, and Agua Mia Delivery. Responses are submitted through the portal and held in the secure Postbox until the deadline for responses has expired. Nominated members of the buyer organisation then unlock the Postbox to access the submissions. The Postbox can be used for the receipt of PQQs, tender responses, Quick Quote submissions and all supporting documents. A full audit trail is kept of all access to the Postbox and a complete record of all supplier submissions is stored. The Postbox is an online submission facility which allows buyers to receive responses from suppliers electronically in a secure environment. Responses are submitted through the portal and held in the secure Postbox until the deadline for responses has expired. Nominated members of the buyer organisation then unlock the Postbox to access the submissions. The Postbox can be used for the receipt of PQQs, tender responses, Quick Quote submissions and all supporting documents. A full audit trail is kept of all access to the Postbox and a complete record of all supplier submissions is stored. Please note: Before you can use the postbox you must record your interest in a notice. In the case of a Quick Quote or the second stage of a dual stage procedure you must have been invited by the buyer to submit a response. Postbox Response Workspace All postbox re

The National Park Service (NPS) reserves the right to purchase materials directly to reduce costs when applicable. There is no limit on the number of site visits. All work requires a written quote submitted by the awardee and approved in writing by the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) before any work is performed. Materials procured by the contractor are subject to a maximum 20% markup, and all receipts must be provided to document compliance. 2. BACKGROUND The National Park Service requires electrical system inspection and repair services for twenty (20) buildings and associated grounds within the National Parks of Boston, located primarily at the Charlestown Navy Yard with additional sites at Bunker Hill Monument and Dorchester Heights. The Government anticipates an acquisition strategy of full and open competition on SAM.gov for this requirement and resulting solicitation, however, the acquisition strategy has not been fully formed and defined. In accordance with RFO Part 10, Market Research, AFLCMC/ESGS is seeking information for potential sources for a Radio Frequency 18:1 Power Divider/Combiner (RFPDC). Security Requirements: The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined; however, the Contractor should anticipate working with teams consisting of military, civilian, national partners, and contract personnel from various services and agencies.
